exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Planning a Survival Story
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Let's write a survival story together. Where should we set it?
Leo: How about Antarctica? The cold there is a real danger.
Mia: Good idea. So our hero is alone on the ice. What dangers does he face?
Leo: The freezing wind, no food, and no way to call for help.
Mia: How does he stay alive?
Leo: He builds a shelter from snow and melts ice for water.
Mia: And how does he feel?
Leo: Frightened at first, but he stays calm and never gives up hope.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 和 Leo 一起写求生故事;他们把背景定在南极,因为那里的严寒是真正的危险;主人公独自在冰上,面对刺骨寒风、没有食物、无法求救;他用雪搭建庇护所、把冰融化成水;一开始害怕,但保持冷静、从不放弃希望。

questions.stem: Where do Mia and Leo decide to set their story?
Why do they choose that place?
options: It is full of friendly people.
The freezing cold is a real danger.
It is easy to find food there.
It is close to their school.

questions.stem: How does the hero get water?
options: He buys it from a shop.

questions.stem: What does the hero build for shelter?
How does the hero feel by the end?
options: He stays calm and keeps hoping.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 Animals in Our Cities
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: More and more wild animals are moving into our cities.
Foxes, racoons and even wild pigs now live among us.
As cities become greener, they offer good places for animals to live.
With fewer natural predators around, these newcomers often do very well.
Hungry animals also find plenty to eat in the food we throw away.
exercises.translation_cn: 越来越多的野生动物迁入我们的城市;狐狸、浣熊甚至野猪如今与我们共处;随着城市变得更绿,它们为动物提供了好的栖身之所;由于天敌更少,这些新来者往往过得很好;饥饿的动物也能在我们丢弃的食物里找到很多吃的。

questions.stem: What is happening to wild animals, according to the passage?
options: They are all kept in zoos.
They are moving into our cities.

questions.stem: Which animals are mentioned?
Why do greener cities suit the animals?
options: They are quieter than the sea.
They offer good places to live.
They have no people at all.

questions.stem: Why do these newcomers often do well?
options: They are fed by the government.

questions.stem: Where do hungry animals find food?
options: In the food people throw away.

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 A Snake Bite in the Wild
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: Help! A snake just bit Tom's leg while we were hiking.
Guide: Stay calm. Keep him still so the poison spreads slowly.
Anna: Should I try to suck out the poison?
Guide: No, never do that. Just clean the wound and cover it.
Anna: And then what?
Guide: We must get him to hospital as quickly as we can.
Anna: I'm so glad you knew what to do.
Guide: Whenever you go into the wild, it helps to know basic first aid.
exercises.translation_cn: 远足时一条蛇咬了 Tom 的腿;向导让 Anna 保持冷静、让 Tom 别动好让毒液扩散得慢些;Anna 问要不要把毒吸出来,向导说绝对不要,只需清理伤口并盖好;接着要尽快把他送到医院;向导说每次进野外都该懂些基本急救。

questions.stem: What happened to Tom?
What does the guide tell Anna to do first?
options: Stay calm and keep Tom still.

questions.stem: Should Anna suck out the poison?
options: No, she should never do that.

questions.stem: What must they do next?
What does the guide advise about the wild?
options: Learn basic first aid before you go.
Never go into the wild again.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 Birds and Glass
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many birds cannot tell the difference between the open sky and clear glass.
Because of this, they fly straight into the windows of tall city buildings.
Scientists estimate that huge numbers of birds die this way every year.
Some kinds of birds are hurt much more than others.
They have not yet changed the old routes that take them through our cities.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多鸟分不清开阔的天空和透明的玻璃;因此它们径直撞向城市高楼的窗户;科学家估计每年有大量鸟因此死亡;有些种类的鸟受害远比其他鸟严重;它们还没有改变那些带它们穿过城市的古老路线。

questions.stem: Why do many birds fly into windows?
options: They cannot tell the sky from clear glass.
They want to enter the buildings.

questions.stem: What kind of buildings does this happen at?
What do scientists estimate?
options: That the danger is now gone.
That only one bird dies a year.
That huge numbers of birds die each year.

questions.stem: Are all kinds of birds hurt equally?
Why are some birds hurt more than others?
options: Their old routes still lead them through cities.
They are too small to see glass.

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Talking about Robinson Crusoe
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sam: I've just finished Robinson Crusoe. What a survival story!
Kate: I think so too. He spends years alone on a desert island.
Sam: What helps him survive, do you think?
Kate: His calmness and patience, I believe. He never panics.
Sam: That's true. He also makes his own tools and grows his own food.
Kate: The way I see it, his clever and hopeful mind matters most.
Sam: I can't agree more. We can all learn from him in a crisis.
Kate: No matter how hard things get, he keeps on trying.
exercises.translation_cn: Sam 刚读完《鲁滨逊漂流记》,觉得是了不起的求生故事;Kate 也这么认为,主人公在荒岛上独自生活多年;两人讨论是什么帮他活下来;Kate 认为是冷静和耐心,他从不惊慌;Sam 补充他还自制工具、自己种粮食;Kate 觉得最重要的是他聪明而充满希望的头脑;两人一致认为无论多难,他都坚持不懈。

questions.stem: What book have Sam and Kate read?
Where does the man in the story live?
What qualities help him survive, in Kate's view?
What does the man make and grow for himself?
What lesson do Sam and Kate draw from him?
options: It is better to give up early.
We can learn from him in a crisis.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 A Tip for a Crisis
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is one simple tip for facing any crisis.
First, stay calm, because panic only makes things worse.
Next, look closely at what you have and what you really need.
Then make a clear plan, one small step at a time.
No matter how hard the situation seems, a calm and hopeful mind will help you find a way through.
exercises.translation_cn: 这里有一个应对任何危机的简单贴士:第一,保持冷静,因为惊慌只会让情况更糟;第二,仔细看看你拥有什么、真正需要什么;然后制定清晰的计划,一次走一小步;无论情况看起来多难,冷静而充满希望的心态都会帮你找到出路。

questions.stem: What is the first thing to do in a crisis?
Why should you not panic?
What should you look closely at?
options: What you have and really need.

questions.stem: How should you make your plan?
options: All at once in a hurry.
One small step at a time.

questions.stem: What will help you find a way through?
